calculator: Time is the secret ingredient of compound interest.
A little every month beats a lot once in a while.
Income tax drops with each deposit's age: patience pays.
Passive income is money working for you. At 1% a month, R$ 100k pays R$ 1,000.
The math turns it around: what you want ÷ the monthly yield = what you need to have.
Reinvesting the payouts is the secret: what was earned also earns, and the time shrinks.

community: Found a bug? Tell me on r/VisionDungeon.

Community tips show up down here.
fii_fixed: Think of a REIT as rent landing every month, tax-free. Fixed income follows the CDI, but is taxed.
Here I put both in the same language: what each pays a month, after tax.
If the REIT pays less than the "tie", fixed income would earn more, without the share's ups and downs.
Past payouts don't promise the future: an empty building or a tenant who doesn't pay cuts the REIT.
Fixed income's tax drops with time: 22.5% up to 6 months, 15% after 2 years. That's why I ask how long.
LCI and LCA are tax-free too, like REITs for individuals. Compare tax-free with tax-free!
magic_number: Snowball: when one month's payout buys a new share by itself, out of nobody's pocket.
Like a tree that drops a new seed every month. The more trees, the faster the orchard grows.
The math is share price ÷ payout per share. A R$ 100 share paying R$ 1? That's 100 shares.
If the payout drops or the price rises, the number changes. Use it as a goal, not a promise.
Once the snowball rolls, each new share raises the payout, and the snowball speeds up.
price_ceiling: A price ceiling is a limit: how much to pay for a stock so it still makes sense by one rule.
Bazin wanted 6% a year in dividends. If the company paid R$ 3 a share, he'd pay up to R$ 50.
Graham blended profit and book value: at most 15 times earnings and 1.5 times book value.
They're old, simple methods. They don't know the company's future: use them as a starting point.
Below the ceiling doesn't mean "buy", above doesn't mean "sell". It's a ruler, not an order.

help.BUDGET:
Build the month's plan: where each part of the income goes.

• Income: the one registered in the app (Household income) or your own number, to simulate.
• Slices as % of income or in R$ (e.g. 10% savings, 20% leisure, fixed expenses in R$).
• Tie a slice to a category and, when you save, it becomes that category's spending cap.

The saved plan shows on Home ("Monthly plan").

Terms:
• Unassigned: the part of the income the plan hasn't set aside for anything.
• Planned × done: what the plan expected and what really happened.
• Cost of living: fixed expenses plus your average other spending.
help.INCOME:
Add each household income: everyone's salary, a freelance job, rent you receive…

• Fixed: the monthly amount.
• Hourly: hourly rate × hours per day × business days of the cycle (no weekends or national holidays).

The cycle runs from payday (in Settings) to the day before the next one. On Home, "Income and leftover" shows what's left after fixed expenses.
help.HOME:
Here's the summary of your treasure.

• Net worth: how much your chests are worth today, after income tax and IOF.
• Earned yesterday / this month: the net yield, calculated with the official CDI rate from Brazil's Central Bank.
• Achievements and goals: months in a row saving, financial freedom (how much of the fixed expenses the yield pays) and each goal's progress.
• Upcoming bills and today's news.

At the top: the newspaper opens the news (and from there the community), the eye hides the amounts so nobody peeks, and the gear opens the settings.

"Customize home", at the bottom, chooses what shows up here and in what order. Tap the dragon to make it talk!
help.POCKETS:
Chests are the investments you already have at your bank: CDB, RDB, Tesouro, yielding accounts…

Create one for each goal, with the % of CDI it pays and an optional goal. The app calculates the yield day by day, with income tax and IOF for each deposit by its age. The chest fills up as you approach the goal.

Vision doesn't hold or invest money: the amounts are an estimate. The real amount is always your bank's.

Terms:
• CDI: the benchmark rate for investments; "100% of CDI" earns the same as it.
• Gross: before taxes. Net: what is left after.
• Income tax (IR): on the yield, lower the longer the money stays.
• IOF: a tax only if the money leaves within 30 days.
help.POCKET_DETAIL:
Log what happens in the chest:

• Deposit: money that came in.
• Withdrawal: type the amount that reached your account; the app takes out the taxes.
• Adjustment: when the bank's balance is different, enter the gross balance and the difference becomes yield.

"Simulate" opens the calculator with today's balance. The "Yield forecast" estimates the yield per day, month and year; "See details" shows how often it pays each fixed expense and how much more to save for it to pay every month.
help.POCKET_FORM: Name, bank, type (taxed or tax-free, like LCI/LCA and savings) and how much of CDI it pays. The goal is optional. If you change the % later, the app asks from when it applies.
help.BILLS:
Fixed expenses: rent, electricity, internet, subscriptions…

Add the expected amount and the due day. You get a reminder before it's due (the time is in Settings). When you pay, enter the real amount: the app keeps the history and the average. Next month the expense comes back as pending on its own.

Filter by "To pay" and "Paid". "Entries", next to it, is the day-to-day tracker (can be turned off in Settings).

Financing installments (Loans → I owe) are in the "Financiamentos" group: marking one paid counts the installment. On the chart, the corner button switches between % and R$.
help.SPENDING:
Your day-to-day entries, only on your phone: money in and money out.

• The period follows payday (in Settings), like the fixed expenses.
• New entry: amount, description, date and account. On a card it can be split into installments (by the total or by the installment).
• Bank notifications: pick each account's bank in ⚙ Accounts and cards, and purchases and Pix become entries on their own.
• ⚙ Import: an OFX/CSV statement or a screenshot of the bill; repeated ones are skipped, and installments already go into the coming bills.
• Tap an entry to edit it, split it or tie it to a fixed expense (or make a new one from it).
• Automatic category from the description (iFood → Food…). Fixed it? The app offers to remember.
• Card bill payments, investments and transfers don't count as spending (change it in ⚙ Categories).
• Search by description, category or amount. On the charts, the corner button switches between % and R$.
• Caps: per account/card and per category, with a warning at 80% and 100%. New spending counts.

Terms:
• Spending: everything that hit the period, with installments of older purchases and the fixed expenses paid.
• New spending: only what you bought in the period (no installments of older purchases or fixed expenses).
• Not spending: money that only moved (paying the card bill, saving, transferring).
• By date: when you bought. By bill: when the card charges.
• Cap: the most you want to spend a month in that account or category.
help.ACCOUNTS: Where your money is: bank account, credit card or cash. Each one can have a monthly cap: I warn you when it gets close and when it goes over. For a card, enter the day the bill closes and the day it's due to see the open bill in Spending.
help.RULES: Caps per category (how much you can spend per month on Leisure, Food…) and your categorization rules: a description with the word goes to the chosen category. Your rules come before the ones built into the app.
help.BILL_FORM: Expected amount, due day (in a short month it falls on the last day) and category. An empty "Remind how many days before" uses the default from Settings. Turning it off keeps the history without reminders.
help.LOANS:
Two tabs:

• Owed to me: a Pix or a loan (at once or in installments) or an installment purchase on your card for someone else. The app creates the installments, reminds you of each one and writes the reminder message.
• I owe: your financings (house, car, a bank loan). Each one becomes a boss with a life bar, and its installment a fixed expense with a reminder.

Everything can be edited later (the pencil at the top). It's just a personal note: Vision doesn't charge or move money.
help.LOAN_DETAIL:
Mark each installment received or log a repayment. The total owed drops on its own, and the reminders stop when everything is paid.

The pencil edits the person, the description and the number of installments (received ones stay). Tap an installment still to receive to fix its amount or due date.
help.LOAN_FORM: To whom, what and how much. With installments, enter how many and the 1st due date; if you only know the installment, choose "I know the installment" and the total works itself out. Interest per month is optional (Price table). Started earlier? Say how many were already paid. On a card, the purchase can also go to the spending tracker.
help.FINANCING:
The boss is your debt: its life bar is what's left to pay. It goes from red to green, and when it's paid off the boss turns into coins.

• Each installment marked paid in Fixed expenses is a hit; you're told at half and when it's paid off.
• Update from the bank statement: copy the balance owed and the installments left from the bank app. With the bill's amount, the app finds the month's TR.
• An extra payment goes straight to the balance: see how much you save shortening the term or lowering the installment, and whether amortizing beats leaving it in a chest.
• Simulate: moving to another bank and paying the last installments now.
• Insurance and fees go into the installment but don't pay the debt down.

The numbers are an estimate by the Price or SAC table: update from the statement now and then.
help.FINANCING_FORM:
Take the numbers from the contract or the bank app: amount financed, interest, term and the system (Price or SAC).

• Interest: "nominal/yr" is what contracts usually show ("nominal interest").
• Correction: TR or IPCA, if the contract has one.
• Installments already paid: only the ones paid in order, up to the last one due. Paid some from the end? Use the bank's numbers (balance owed and installments left).
• Charges: the bill's insurance and administration fee.

The installment becomes a fixed expense with a reminder.
help.TOOLS: Calculators to decide better: compound interest with income tax, loan amortization (and whether amortizing beats investing), REITs and stocks, and splitting the bill with friends.
help.CALCULATOR: How money grows over time. Enter the initial amount, the monthly deposit, the term and the rate (% of CDI or % per year). The result already takes out the income tax of each deposit by its age. Like the final amount? Create a chest with that goal.
help.AMORTIZATION:
Simulate a financing or loan with Price (fixed installment) or SAC (installment that drops). The rate can be per month, nominal per year (as in contracts) or effective per year.

Add an extra every month and/or a one-time extra in one month (bonus…) to see how many months less and how much interest you save. "Pay it down or let it earn?" compares, spending the same per month, with investing the extra in your chests.

Terms:
• Price: equal installments from start to end.
• SAC: installments that start bigger and keep dropping.
• Paying down: an extra that goes straight to the debt.
help.SPLIT: Split a bill among friends, with an optional service fee and adjustments per person. The app writes the message for the group with your Pix key (in Settings) and can turn each part into a loan to remember who still has to pay.
help.NEWS: Finance headlines (Valor and Money Times, in Portuguese). "Relevant" sorts the last week by what affects your pocket the most: Selic, CDI, savings, income tax, inflation… "Recent" shows everything by date. Tap to read on the site.
help.COMMUNITY: r/VisionDungeon on Reddit is the place to report bugs, suggest ideas and dragon skins, and swap tips. Posts with the flair "📈 Dicas de Economia / Rendimentos" show up here.
help.SETTINGS:
• Your dragon: choose which one guards the treasure; new ones come with achievements or a short video.
• Spending tracker, fingerprint/PIN on open, daily notification time and reminders.
• Backup: automatic to your Google Drive or to a file, to take to another device.
help.ACHIEVEMENTS:
Medals you earn saving and making the treasure grow: net worth, yield, months in a row saving, emergency fund, goals reached and more. Each one has a metal, and the next one shows at the top.

Terms:
• Cost of living: fixed expenses plus the average of your spending in the last 3 months.
• Financial freedom: how much of the cost of living the chests' yield already pays.
• Reserve: how many months of the cost of living the emergency chest covers.
help.MONTH_REPORT: The summary of a period (from payday to the day before the next): expected income, fixed expenses paid, other spending, how much went into the chests and how much the treasure earned, against the previous month. The chart shows where the spending went. "Share summary" sends it to whoever you like.
help.HOLDING:
A REIT (tower) or stock (mine) you hold: shares, average price, what it's worth today and what it yields.

Log purchases, sales and payouts for the app to work out the average price, the profit or loss on sales and the payouts per month. "Change price" updates the quote, and the alerts tell you when it reaches the buy or sell price you choose.
help.INVESTING:
Sums to understand REITs and stocks, not advice to buy or sell:

• Does this REIT pay more than fixed income? Compares the share's payout with a CDB at the same % of the CDI, after income tax.
• Snowball: how many shares until the fund gives you a new share every month.
• A stock's ceiling price: up to what price it still makes sense by classic methods.

With the ticker, the app opens its numbers on Status Invest. Tap the dragon for another explanation.
